items.q: For most build decisions, 'what's best' usually:
options: Depends on your goal — the options trade off against each other (simple vs. flexible, cheap vs. scalable)
Has one correct answer the AI already knows
Doesn't matter, so just accept the first suggestion

explain.right: Options are better at some things and worse at others; naming the tradeoff lets you choose with eyes open.
explain.wrong: There's rarely one right answer, 'newest' isn't automatically best, and accepting the first option blindly hides the tradeoff.

items.q: Which decision should a human keep, rather than hand fully to the AI?
options: Deleting real user data, spending money, or deploying publicly

explain.right: Security, real data, money, and irreversible actions are decisions of consequence the human owns.
explain.wrong: Naming, indentation, and comment style are low-stakes and reversible — fine to delegate.

items.q: Why keep irreversible, security, money, and data decisions with the human?
options: The AI isn't smart enough to understand them
The AI predicts plausible actions, and plausible isn't the same as safe — especially for things you can't undo
Humans are simply faster at deciding

explain.right: A model generates likely-looking actions; for consequential, can't-undo steps you want human judgment, not just plausibility.
explain.wrong: It's not about raw intelligence, law, or speed — it's that plausible output can still be unsafe or irreversible.

items.q: What does 'staying in the loop' on a consequential change mean in practice?
options: Understand it well enough to restate it before approving; do it in small reversible steps and commit first
Let the AI auto-approve its own changes
Approve quickly so you keep momentum

explain.right: If you can't explain it in your own words, don't approve it yet — and keep a commit so it's reversible.
explain.wrong: Rubber-stamping or auto-approving defeats the point, and you don't have to avoid risk entirely — just stay the decider.

items.q: Name one decision you'd never fully hand to the AI, and say why.
rubric: Names a security, real-data, money, or irreversible decision (e.g. deleting user data, deploying publicly, a payment)
Explains the stakes: can't be undone / safety / cost / real people's data
Implies the human should decide/approve it, with the AI advising at most

explain.right: Strong answers pick a consequential, hard-to-undo action and explain the stakes that make it the human's call.
explain.wrong: A weak answer names a trivial, reversible choice (like a variable name) that's fine to delegate.
